result:
I found 12 rules where the code didn't match the docstring and fixed them all in `pricebook.py`. After the fixes, I checked all 150 rules against a reference calculation built from each docstring and the module's shared rules. It used quantities 0–399 at ten unit prices, plus the negative-input check. No rule disagreed, and `quote` still raises `KeyError` for an unknown id.

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 17, 44, 50 | `round()` rounded the discount instead of flooring it to the won | Changed to `// 100` (floor) |
| 43 | Threshold was 21 instead of 20 | `qty >= 20` |
| 56 | Threshold was 51 instead of 50 | `qty >= 50` |
| 46, 57 | The cap was applied to the amount before the percentage, not to the discount | Calculate the discount first, then cap it with `min(disc, cap)` |
| 49, 134 | The cap only applied when the discount was over 60,000 won | Always cap with `min(disc, 30000)` |
| 61 | Rate was 13% instead of 12% | 12 |
| 74 | Rate was 8% instead of 7% | 7 |
| 127 | Rate was 3% instead of 2% | 2 |

STATUS: DONE
